questions.q: Why does Flow Designer need a dedicated 'Ask for Approval' action family instead of just using Create Record and Update Record?
options: Because approvals require the flow to genuinely pause execution and wait on a real human decision, not run straight through
Because Create Record and Update Record are incapable of touching approval tables
Because approvals are purely cosmetic and don't need any real waiting
Because notifications already pause a flow on their own
questions.explain: Approval actions model real stop-and-wait behavior; the other actions all execute immediately with no pause.

questions.q: In a 'group — anyone' approval, how does the step resolve?
options: Whichever single group member responds first resolves the whole step
Every member of the group must respond before it resolves
Only a named individual, never a group, can resolve it
It resolves automatically after a fixed time with no human input
questions.explain: Group-anyone approvals resolve on the first response from any qualified member of the group.

questions.q: What real record type does an approval action create for each approver to interact with?
options: sysapproval_approver
sys_notification
sys_flow_context
sysapproval_group
questions.explain: sysapproval_approver is the actual approval record each approver sees and acts on, the same type used by the Approvals module elsewhere on the platform.

questions.q: A change advisory board decision needs every board member to sign off before implementation proceeds. Which approval variant fits?
options: Approval from a group — everyone
Approval from a group — anyone
Approval from a specific individual
No approval action — use Update Record instead
questions.explain: Group-everyone requires every member to approve, matching a genuinely collective decision like a CAB sign-off.

questions.q: What typically follows an approval action in a well-built flow?
options: An If/Else condition that branches on whether the approval was approved or rejected
Nothing — the approval action itself updates all downstream records automatically
Another approval action, since one approval can never be enough
A For-Each loop over every rejected approver
questions.explain: The approval action only produces an outcome; branching logic (Lesson 6's If/Else) decides what the flow does with that outcome.
